According to the “trustless arbitration” they praise in their whitepaper, a random passerby—or even a competitor—could write some wild script and submit a zero-knowledge proof into the TaskManager contract, accusing the operation of being flawed. This isn’t coding at all; it’s Solidity used to reshape the industry’s unspoken rules. #newt <t-10/>

#newt Don’t get fooled into a limp by the so-called “sunshine compliance.” Take a careful look at the underlying architecture of @NewtonProtocol —those hidden landmines inside are absolutely not something minor. The compliance receipts they produce are, in substance, not a pass-issued document at all, but a “cyber tattoo” permanently welded onto the chain. As soon as any transfer touches the risk-control engine, the system immediately packages the intercepted details, verification signatures, and block coordinates, and hard-codes them deep into the mainnet. So what does this mean? Your record of getting blocked becomes public black history. $ETH #ETH 

In the past, when you hit a bottleneck at a physical bank, you could at least argue at the counter and file an appeal. But in the decentralized world, once this kind of electronic shackles is generated, there’s nowhere to reason with them. In the future, any on-chain sleuth or trading counterparty only needs to input an address to follow the trail and dig out all your stains. What’s most deadly is that even a block caused merely by personal verification not being updated in time is, in the machine’s eyes, indistinguishable in severity from money laundering. They can arbitrarily blacklist you, and you have no way to defend yourself.

As for the “zero privacy leaks” claim in their whitepaper—it's pure conceptual sleight of hand. Your real name may not be exposed, but the rejected application history is laid bare across the entire network. Under this system, even if you’re a law-abiding citizen, once you’ve been tagged with something suspicious even once, it becomes extremely difficult to survive in this ecosystem afterward. Watching $NEWT ’s market trend climb steadily to $1.20, an invisible credit shackle is quietly taking shape. Future smart contracts don’t care who you are—they only care whether you have a prior record. Once they spot a flaw, they simply refuse service.

To survive in this dark web, you have to be willing to sever a limb: the core vault where you store large funds absolutely must have no ties whatsoever with this kind of censorship-based protocol. Be honest and break up your trades on a pure, censorship-resistant decentralized exchange—never give Newton any chance to collect and map your behavioral track record.

Date: 2026-07-02

Tonight, there’s no rush to bet on direction.
The BTC 60,000 integer level is being held for now, but this looks more like sentiment follow-through after panic orders swapped and rotated—not a right-side reversal signal. The “blood pack” released by the AI compute narrative’s sharp selloff has been absorbed by BTC and part of the SOL ecosystem, but getting taken doesn’t mean it can stand firm.

【Today’s Main Call】
The 60,000 psychological level still needs one more non-decreasing-volume confirmation.
Until price truly regains and holds back above 61,000 on expanding volume, the short-side setup remains unchanged. Today’s Non-Farm Payrolls data is that “late hammer”—it could accelerate a fast drop, or it could confirm absorption. Don’t jump in early to gamble on direction.

【Three Main Lines】

BTC｜The Anchor for the Whole Market
At around 61,229.5, price is hovering. Overhead resistances: 61,688 / 62,000 / 63,000. Downside supports: 60,500 / 59,700 / 58,000. The facts are clear: June closed down 20.5%, the worst monthly performance since 2022. The Fear & Greed Index is at 19, in the extreme fear zone. The good news is that someone is buying—Japan-listed Metaplanet increased its position by 2,823 coins against the trend, and a whale placed long orders near 58,243 with a stop-loss at 57,792. The bad news is that Binance’s BTC balance has risen slightly by 560 coins over the past hour, meaning the existing supply remains high.

My plan: 59,700–60,500 is the long/short dividing zone. Don’t chase longs here. Wait for a 1H candle close above 61,000 with volume expansion before considering that the short-side weakness is fading. If there’s a retest that doesn’t break 59,700, you can try a small long position. Targets: 61,688–62,000. If it breaks below 57,800 with volume, stop all left-side attempts.

ETH｜A Weak Market
At 1,644.82, ETH is drifting weakly. Today Binance ETH wallets added 22,128 coins, bringing the total to 3.196 million. Exchange supply pressure is rising. But what’s interesting is that the whale 0x2684 withdrew all 15,802 ETH from Binance within two days and staked it. Whale buying and retail selling pressure are currently offsetting each other. The awkward part is that the ETH/BTC ratio continues to weaken—the market treats ETH as a high-volatility BTC Beta, not as an independent narrative.

My plan: 1,500–1,600 is the key support zone. Only if it breaks should you discuss larger structural risks. Don’t add positions actively until a breakout above 1,666. The whale’s staking behavior near 1,590 can only be used as reference, not as a buy signal. Its “chase after price” temperament means the bottom-fishing value is weaker than BTC and SOL.

SOL｜The Only Large Cap with Resilience
At 81.95, SOL is benefiting from a rebound in on-chain meme momentum. The SOL/BTC exchange rate shows resilience stronger than most altcoins. After AI hardware’s hard crash, some active capital flowed into the SOL chain for speculation and cross-play. The new token issuance volume hit a 80-day high, and ANSEM briefly broke above $170 million. But this kind of heat depends heavily on emotional continuity.

My plan: If around 80 there’s a low-volume pullback that doesn’t break the structure, it can be observed as a short-term long opportunity window. 95 is the next psychological level—only a breakout opens more room. But if BTC loses 59,700 again, SOL’s independent行情 (independent trend) is very likely to be dragged down.

AI Power Infrastructure｜A Surviving Theme During the Compute Crash
Bloom Energy and Brookfield expanded the AI power supply cooperation framework from $5 billion to $25 billion. Certainty around power-side capital expenditures is actually increasing. The more the market worries about excess compute, the more upstream power infrastructure is seen as a higher-certainty investment. But note: if big-company Q2 earnings revise down capital expenditures, the power side will also be dragged. Wait for the Q2 earnings season observation window—don’t chase now.

HYPE｜The Protection Umbrella for Those Holding Profit
Some traders moved their stop-loss to breakeven after reaching TP1, entering a floating profit protection state. If you didn’t enter, don’t chase in at this moment—HYPE’s liquidity makes it unsuitable for adding aggressively on panic days.

Before Non-Farm Payrolls, don’t run unhedged high-leverage.

在真正放量站回61000之前，空头格局不变。今天非农数据就是那把迟到的锤子，可能加速快速下跌，也可能确认承接，别提前跳进去赌方向。

BTC｜全场锚
现价61229.5一线晃悠，上方阻力61688/62000/63000，下行支撑60500/59700/58000。盘面事实很清楚：6月收跌20.5%，创2022年以来最差月度表现，恐慌贪婪指数19处于极度恐惧区。好消息是有人接——日本上市公司Metaplanet逆势加仓2823枚，巨鲸在58243附近挂多单进场，止损设在57792。坏消息是币安BTC余额近一小时小幅增加560枚，存量仍高。
我的思路：59700-60500是多空分界区，不在这里追多。耐心等1H实体站上61000并放量，才认为空头走弱。回踩不破59700可轻仓试多，目标61688-62000。如果带量跌破57800，停止一切左侧尝试。

ETH｜弱盘
现价1644.82晃得软绵绵。币安ETH钱包今天增加22128枚，总量升到319.6万枚，交易所存量压力上来了。但有意思的是巨鲸0x2684两天内从币安提走15802枚ETH全部质押，鲸鱼买盘和散户抛压正在对冲。尴尬的是ETH/BTC汇率持续走弱，市场只把ETH当高波动BTC Beta，不认独立叙事。
我的思路：1500-1600是关键支撑区，破了才能聊更大结构性风险。突破1666之前不主动加仓，1590附近的鲸鱼质押行为只能当参考，不是买入信号。跟跌不跟涨的体质，抄底性价比弱于BTC和SOL。

SOL｜唯一有韧性的大票
现价81.95，受益于链上meme热度回暖，SOL/BTC汇率表现出强于大多数山寨的韧性。AI硬件暴跌后，一部分活跃资金涌入SOL链上博弈，新代币发行量创80天新高，ANSEM一度突破1.7亿美元。但这种热度极度依赖情绪持续性。

HYPE｜持盈者的保护伞
已有交易员到达TP1后把止损移至保本点，处于浮盈保护状态。没入场的不在此刻追入，HYPE的流动性决定了它不适合恐慌日加仓。

🔄 Ethereum is undergoing its biggest leadership transition in years—EthLabs has been born

This is a piece of news that requires some patience to explain, but it may be more important than many price headlines.

The Ethereum Foundation (EF) recently announced layoffs of 20% and a 40% budget cut—so what happened next?

The core protocol development team separated from the Ethereum Foundation to form a new independent entity: EthLabs.

What is EthLabs’ positioning?

It focuses on research and development of Ethereum’s core protocol, but operates in a more flexible and market-oriented way—no longer relying on the Ethereum Foundation’s budget approvals, with greater autonomy.

CoinDesk describes this as “the biggest leadership transition in Ethereum in years.”

Why does this matter?

Ethereum has long been a subject of debate: is the foundation a cradle of innovation, or a breeding ground for bureaucracy?

The creation of EthLabs, to some extent, acknowledges that the latter criticism may be valid—turning the core team from an “official institution” into an “independent team” could actually be more beneficial for efficiency and innovation.

Of course, independence also means losing the foundation’s credibility endorsement and funding security.

What do you think of Ethereum’s organizational restructuring?👇

【ETH不是普通山寨币，这次跌到位了吗？】

说个有意思的事。

昨天ETH还是$ 1568，今天一看，$ 1644，涨了快5个点。再看一周前呢？基本没动。再往回看一个月？也就那样。

这说明什么？市场在震荡，在等方向。

但我更想聊的是另一个问题——为什么我一直说ETH不是普通山寨币？

打个比方。

BTC像什么？像一块限量版的黄金地段土地。稀缺，永远就那么多。

大多数山寨币呢？像那片土地上的临时摊位。今天能摆，明天可能就被赶走了。热度来得快，去得更快。

那ETH是什么？ETH是建在那块地上的房子。房子本身不值钱，但它能出租、它有功能、有人愿意为它付租金。

以太坊上跑着无数应用、智能合约、DeFi、NFT生态，这些才是ETH真正的价值支撑。币价可以跌，但只要链上活动还在，只要还有人在用以太坊转账、部署合约、质押ETH，那ETH就有底。

当所有人都觉得"完了还要跌"的时候，其实底就不远了。

记住一点：ETH跌的时候，要看它跌的是价格，还是它真正的东西。房子还在、功能还在、地段还在，那就只是打折，不是贬值。

For most people who get robbed on-chain, it’s not that their private keys were stolen—it’s that they signed the transaction themselves. The phishing page looks exactly like the official site. You think you’re minting, you think you’re swapping—but what you actually sign is a full-amount approval being sent to an unknown contract. In the fraction of a second when you sign, no one stops you.

Our protection today, to put it bluntly, largely relies on “reminders”: the security plugin pops up a red warning, someone in the community calls it out, the project team issues an announcement. But reminders are only suggestions. If your finger slips, you can still click “confirm.” And on-chain rules are simple: once you sign, the funds move—there’s no second door. Even if post-incident tracking is excellent, the assets are already in a mixer.

#ETH 
Newton Mainnet Beta’s secure execution domain fills in that missing door before settlement. After you sign a transaction and before the money moves, it runs a real-time threat check: whether the target contract matches known drainer patterns, whether the approval amount is abnormal, and whether this action goes beyond the boundaries you set in advance. If it hits, it blocks it—does not allow it—and writes the “rejected” signing proof to the blockchain.

Note: this is fundamentally different from a plugin reminder. Reminders can’t control your finger slip. Forced enforcement can: even if you really sign, if the policy doesn’t allow it, the transaction never reaches settlement.

$NEWT 
What drives all of this is the operation of this interception network.

#BTC 
Of course, the boundaries must be made clear too: interception depends on how well the policy and threat intelligence are covered. New attack methods may still slip through. It turns “one slip = total loss” into “one slip = a recorded interception,” but it shouldn’t be an excuse for you to sign recklessly. With security, machines guard the door—but you still have to guard your habits yourself.

On-chain access shouldn’t stop at the moment you log in
Today, I’ll keep looking at Newton Mainnet Beta for @NewtonProtocol . I want to look at it from a different angle—not talk about the treasury, and not talk about risk control first.
I’d rather talk about “identity.”
Many on-chain products now also do KYC, whitelists, eligibility checks, and region restrictions. The problem is: these checks often happen right at the entrance—can you log in, can you enter a page, can you click a certain button.#ETH 
But when the assets actually move, the on-chain execution may not remember those rules.
That’s awkward.
The frontend tells you this address meets the requirements; the backend says users like this can participate. But once the transaction reaches the contract layer—what truly determines how funds move—maybe only a set of generic calls remains.
Newton’s identity checks, in my view, aren’t about “verifying one more time.”
The key is to put eligibility checks into policies before transaction execution.
When an intent comes in, it doesn’t only ask: does this wallet have a signature? It can further ask: does this address meet eligibility, is it within the allowed range, does it satisfy KYC/KYB, and does it trigger certain restriction conditions.
And the final result isn’t just a backend conclusion—it’s an on-chain verifiable pass/fail attestation.
That’s quite realistic for DeFi.
If later vaults, RWA, stablecoins, and even AI agents need to connect to more complex fund paths, identity can’t be only a gate on the login page. It should become part of what’s checked every time funds are allowed to move.#BTC 
Of course, there are also issues that need close attention here.
Who defines the identity rules? Where does the eligibility data come from? How do we balance privacy and compliance boundaries? In the Beta stage, how many real scenarios are actually using this?
But I do appreciate the question Newton Mainnet Beta is asking:
On-chain finance can’t just verify “who clicked confirm.” It also needs to verify “right now, whether this person, this address, and this action are actually eligible to execute.”
That’s where I see the future needs for $NEWT .
It’s not about how many people discuss it during an event period—it’s about whether authorization and eligibility checks will become a foundational step that every real transaction has to go through every day.

title: Altcoins Flash Green as Liquidity Rotates Out of BTC Dominance
subTitle:
Something shifted today, and if you have been watching the BTC dominance chart, you already feel it. Bitcoin is up 2.43% over the last 24 hours, sitting at $61,581.99 according to Binance, with $1.39 billion in daily volume per CoinMarketCap. Respectable, but not extraordinary. Meanwhile, Ethereum has quietly outpaced it with a 4.86% push to $1,697.25 on $676.84 million in volume. That kind of divergence is not random noise. It is capital rotating down the risk curve, and the altcoin market is screaming the same story.

Look at today's top movers on CoinMarketCap. M is up 45.2%, B has ripped 22.5%, and LIT has added 17.9%. These are not micro-caps that move on a single whale order. When multiple altcoins across different sectors print double-digit gains on the same day while BTC treads water near resistance, you are looking at a classic altcoin rotation. Liquidity that parked itself in Bitcoin during the recent uncertainty is now hunting for beta, hunting for the next leg higher in risk assets. The tide is turning.

The macro backdrop supports this read. The UK just published a payments blueprint outlining tokenized payments for what they are calling a multi-money ecosystem. That is central bank infrastructure acknowledging blockchain rails as a permanent feature of finance. When regulators build on-chain, the investable universe for crypto expands. Separately, Aave bringing V3 lending and its GHO stablecoin to Monad signals that DeFi infrastructure is not slowing down despite a choppy market. These are not hype narratives. These are fundamental expansions of what crypto can do, and they matter more for altcoin valuations than they do for Bitcoin's store-of-value thesis.

Now let us talk about the levels that actually matter for your next decision. Bitcoin is pressing against $62,200 resistance, the ceiling that has capped price action for the past 72 hours. A clean break above that level on strong volume would confirm that BTC is ready to drag the whole market higher, and altcoins would likely accelerate even faster. But if BTC gets rejected here and fades back toward its $57,800 support, the rotation could stall. That support is the floor where buyers have consistently stepped in over the past three days. If it holds, the structure remains bullish and any dip toward it is the zone where conviction buyers defend. If it loses $57,800, the picture flips bearish quickly, and the altcoin gains printed today could evaporate as liquidity rushes back to the sidelines.

Ethereum tells a tighter story. At $1,697.25, it is sitting just below its $1,725 resistance. ETH has outperformed BTC on a percentage basis today, which is exactly what you want to see in an altcoin rotation. If ETH breaks and holds above $1,725, that opens the door for alt-layers and DeFi tokens to keep running. Its 72h support sits at $1,550.20. As long as that floor holds on any pullback, the uptrend from today's move stays intact. Losing $1,550 would signal that the rotation was a head fake, not a regime shift.

The broader picture is one of global liquidity slowly easing back into risk. The macro upgrades rolling out across blockchain infrastructure, the regulatory signals from the UK, and the DeFi expansion onto new chains like Monad all point to capital finding reasons to stay in crypto rather than leave. Today's rotation from $BTC into $ETH and further down the cap table is the market pricing that in real time.

Watch $62,200 on BTC and $1,725 on ETH. Those are the gates. If they open, the rotation accelerates. If they hold firm, patience becomes the trade. Tap $BTC or $ETH on Binance to set your levels and trade the range.

Not financial advice.

📰 Crypto Market Highlights

1. SEC acknowledges shortcomings in crypto ETF approvals and plans a new asset-neutral mechanism
The latest comments from U.S. SEC officials say the regulator has recognized that handling of crypto ETF approval processes in the past was not ideal, which has affected industry trust. The SEC is currently trying to build a more orderly, standardized, and asset-neutral approval framework to deal with the large number of ETF applications and other innovative products such as predicted-market instruments. If the new mechanism is implemented, it may help improve transparency and predictability for crypto asset management products.

2. Liquidations total $585 million in crypto derivatives over the past 24 hours, with short sellers hit harder
Latest data shows that liquidations across the crypto perpetual/futures derivatives market over the past 24 hours totaled about $585 million, affecting roughly 130,500 people. Approximately $400 million of positions were liquidated on the short side, while about $184 million were liquidated on the long side. The liquidation structure indicates that the recent market rebound has squeezed shorts more severely, with short-term volatility significantly amplified. The concentration of high-leverage capital being forced out also reflects that market sentiment is switching quickly, and trading risk remains elevated.

3. U.S. Bitcoin ETFs continue net outflows, while Ethereum ETFs turn to net inflows in a single day
On-chain monitoring shows that U.S. Bitcoin ETFs recorded a daily net outflow of 6,165 BTC, and a cumulative net outflow of 32,807 BTC over the past seven days—still signaling cautious capital flows. In contrast, Ethereum ETFs saw a daily net inflow of 21,568 ETH, but over the past seven days overall they remain in net outflow of 54,411 ETH. The data suggests mainstream institutional capital has diverged between BTC and ETH: near-term support for ETH has improved, but the sustainability still needs to be observed.

4. A whale’s ETH short positions are liquidated, further amplifying the rebound rally’s volatility
On-chain analysis shows that the whale address “sat0shi777” recently had 31,600 ETH short positions liquidated, worth about $53.5 million—directly becoming one of the “fuel” sources behind ETH’s upside move. According to disclosures, after the price broke above a key liquidation level, the position was closed out passively, and related losses have become quite evident; the whale still holds part of its short exposure. Liquidation of a whale-level position indicates that short-term ETH volatility is intensifying, and it may continue to affect market sentiment and liquidity structure.

5. Saga divests its crypto business, sets up AI Labs to pivot to an AI consumer platform
Blockchain company Saga announced it will sell its cryptocurrency business and establish Saga AI Labs. Going forward, it will focus on an AI consumer platform and the development of proprietary digital characters. Management control over its blockchain network operations will be transferred to an organization under dao5. The official statement says the related AI projects have been deployed with game partners, and will later expand to scenarios such as consumer brands and sports. The move reflects that some Web3 projects are accelerating their transition toward AI, seeking new growth narratives and commercial opportunities.

A single large liquidation can get the market watching $ETH—not because the “gossip level” is high, but because it puts the question of “who’s being forced to buy back” out in the open. Within half an hour, 31,600 ETH short positions were liquidated; the price immediately broke through 1674. Spot is now 1694.89, up +5.86% in 24h. In this kind of rally, sentiment isn’t the key factor—liquidation orders are the fuel.

I’m not chasing longs right now. I’ve placed a 5% trial short above 1698, stop-loss at 1728, and my first target is 1660. The logic is simple: derivatives trading volume is 11.41 billion, spot volume is 690 million; the derivatives/spot ratio is 16.5x. That suggests leverage is still doing most of the pushing, not spot gradually picking things up. The other short liquidation price is at 1764—still some distance from the current price. The market will likely make a story around that level, but until it gets there, it’s not my chasing point.

The funding rate is only +0.0074%, not extreme, which means the longs haven’t squeezed hot yet. The problem is that the positions haven’t clearly been cleaned out—OI is still 2.366 million ETH. This kind of market is most prone to a two-step move: first, borrow the liquidations to yank price upward; then the people chasing longs finish by taking the last baton. What I want is the spot for the second leg of the spike—not the passive buyback window of the first leg.

If the 1725 high is directly held and solidified, I’ll admit I’m wrong on this short; if the structure changes, I’ll flip. $ETH #ETH

The market is changing—what works today might not work for tomorrow.

Mint Brother wants to tell a story from 2019. Back then, I had only just entered this industry.

Going from 100U to 10000U took just one day. But what truly changed me wasn’t that day.

If time could be turned back, I would definitely tell that version of myself who only had 100U: Don’t rush—opportunities really will come.
In the past, my account would fluctuate—make a little, lose a little—and every day I was doubting myself.

It wasn’t until later that I started taking every single trade seriously.
No more entering trades based on hunch. No more emotional decisions. And no more fantasies that you’d get an opportunity every day.

Then, that day finally arrived.
I didn’t chase and kill like before. Instead, I patiently waited for the trading opportunity that belonged to me.

After entering, the market gradually moved toward my expectations.
I didn’t rush to exit just because I had a small floating profit. I managed my position according to my plan, adjusting step by step as the market changed.

Hours passed, and the numbers in my account kept changing.
When my balance broke through 10000U, I stared at the screen for a long time.

There was no wild, imagined chaos—just an unusually calm feeling.
Because I knew what other people saw was only a day.

Only I know that behind this one day were countless late-night reviews, countless stop-losses, and countless times of overturning myself—until the result finally arrived.

Later, many people asked me:
“Was it enough to catch one market move?” My answer has always been the same:
The truly difficult part isn’t that day.

It’s whether, before that day comes, you have the patience to turn yourself into someone who can actually seize opportunities.
The market is always there every day, but opportunities that belong to you aren’t many.

Instead of thinking about doubling every day, learn to wait, to execute, and to restrain yourself first.
Very often, what really changes your life isn’t a single trade—it’s from some day onward, when you finally stop letting emotions carry you away.

Looking back now, going from 100U to 10000U is more like a long-overdue answer sheet.
It proves that it wasn’t luck—it was persistence.
Opportunities always appear, but only those who are prepared can see them.

title: ETH Rallied 4.5% Today and Nobody Told the ETF Crowd
subTitle:
Ethereum just logged one of its cleaner moves in weeks. At the time of writing, $ETH sits at $1,697.07 on Binance, up 4.53% over the last 24 hours, with $680.31 million in daily volume and a market cap north of $204 billion, per CoinMarketCap. Somewhere, a fund manager is staring at his Bloomberg terminal wondering why nobody called him first.

The number is real. The mood, though, is complicated.

Let us talk about what actually happened before the champagne gets opened. ETH spent the better part of the last several sessions grinding sideways in a range that made even the most committed degenerate consider taking up gardening. Then today, a clean thrust upward that pushed the price right into the neighborhood of the 72h resistance at $1,725. That is not a breakout yet. That is a knock on the door. Whether the door opens or slams back is the only question that matters right now.

The on-chain picture tells a familiar story. Ethereum's network activity has been quietly rebuilding through mid-2026, driven less by speculative frenzy and more by the slow, grinding adoption of real-world asset tokenization and programmable finance infrastructure. Just this week, Ondo expanded its tokenized equities offering with onchain shareholder voting, a signal that institutional-grade plumbing is being laid on Ethereum and its L2s in real time. Meanwhile, the UK payments blueprint outlined plans for tokenized payments within what they call a "multi-money ecosystem," and The biggest blockchain upgrades still to come in 2026 headlines are doing the rounds, reminding everyone that Ethereum's roadmap is far from finished.

None of this moves the price today. All of it moves the price over the next eighteen months. The market, however, is famously allergic to patience.

Here is where the ETF flow conversation gets interesting. Traditional finance has a talent for showing up late and acting early. Spot ETH ETF inflows and outflows have been choppy over recent weeks, reflecting a broader institutional posture that can best be described as "cautious optimism with one foot out the door." When ETH was scraping around near its 72h support of $1,550.20, the flow data showed indifference. Now that the price has rallied nearly five percent in a single session, the phones start ringing. This is how smart money behaves when it is not being particularly smart.

If $ETH holds above the $1,725 resistance level on a closing basis and volume stays elevated, the technical setup flips constructive. That would mean buyers absorbed the overhead supply and the path of least resistance shifts upward, opening a fresh range to explore. Traders watching $ETH should mark that level clearly on their chart and look for confirmation through a sustained close, not just a wick.

If $ETH fails at $1,725 and rolls over, the first real test comes back at $1,550.20. That 72h support is the floor that has to hold to keep the current structure intact. A clean loss of $1,550.20 on meaningful volume would signal that today's rally was a relief bounce rather than a regime change, and sellers would likely reassert control. The $ETH pair on Binance is where you want to watch that play out in real time, with the order book showing you exactly where liquidity is sitting on either side.

The broader context matters too. Notable movers today include M up 47.9%, MAGMA up 40.5%, and SLX up 27.1%, per CoinMarketCap. When smaller caps rip like that while the majors inch higher, it often reads as risk appetite expanding at the edges. That can be bullish for ETH if it flows back into quality. It can also be the froth that precedes a pullback. The market does not hand out cheat sheets.

One more thing worth noting: the FBI director's disclosure of Strategy holdings, which came months after the reporting deadline according to Cointelegraph, is a reminder that regulatory transparency in crypto remains a work in progress. It does not directly move $ETH, but it colors the institutional sentiment that drives ETF allocation decisions. When the rules feel uncertain, allocators move slower. That is just human nature wearing a suit.

So here is the honest read. Ethereum is at a technically interesting spot, the on-chain fundamentals are quietly strengthening, and institutional adoption through tokenization is progressing even if the price does not always reflect it. The 4.53% daily gain is nice. But the real test is whether $1,725 becomes support or a ceiling. Everything else is commentary.

Do you think this rally has enough legs to break $1,725 convincingly, or are we about to get another lesson in resistance rejection? I genuinely want to know.

Laugh, then look at the chart.

Every generation of Apple products, Huaqiangbei always gets the materials in advance.

After each generation of Apple products is released, you can quickly buy accessories online like tempered glass screen protectors and phone cases.

For Huaqiangbei, the leaked information isn’t a big deal; it helps smartphone manufacturers a lot.

But it’s also quite minimal. Back when I was a process engineer on Apple’s production line, there were manufacturers who contacted headhunters to recruit people from us.

Apple’s products rely on design, management, and stringent inspection standards—these domestic manufacturers can hardly meet expectations.

Apple will redo an entire set of molds and the production process because of something as minor as whether a screw might cause slight internal scratches; other manufacturers can’t do that.

For a single scratch caused by a screw, just the tools and process upgrades can require tens of millions in remediation funding.

Back then, for a certain Apple product, I was involved end-to-end in the very first set of processes. If there were issues—adhesive problems, screw problems, inspection equipment problems, workflow problems—they would change them immediately. Many of them involved equipment worth over ten million, and they would reorganize it on the spot. The product launch was delayed because of manufacturing defects, and everything was sealed and stored.

When I communicated with their engineers, it was very straightforward: if there were any issues, as long as you raised them, they would fix them.

At the time, I should have been the only person who could be greeted in person by their engineers whenever they saw me.

Apple’s process flow and systems engineering—every step costs enormous financial resources. Every time someone takes apart an Apple phone, it’s like taking apart a work of art.

Dragonfly Partners: ETH and SOL will “overdeliver,” and new L1s may struggle to deliver

📍 Background

Dragonfly managing partner Haseeb Qureshi spoke again on X, clearly stating that he remains bullish on both ETH and SOL. He believes the crypto industry is not moving toward “centralization” (i.e., middlemen taking over). Instead, some participants exiting is a form of industry filtering—similar to the normal “clean-up” after the early tech bubble burst, leaving behind those who truly believe in long-term value. Short-term pain, long-term upside.

📋 Core Breakdown

1. ETH and SOL will “overdeliver”—even as new networks keep emerging, these two chains will still lead
2. New fintech brands L1s (e.g., Tempo, Arc, Robinhood Chain) may “underdeliver” on key metrics such as daily active addresses, stablecoin liquidity, RWA, and more
3. The best developers will continue building on already-proven neutral chains rather than chasing new chains endorsed by enterprises
4. Haseeb compares ETH to “Microsoft in crypto”—an ecosystem that’s mature and deeply liquid, but with a slower development cadence

🔑 Core Logic Analysis

Haseeb’s bullish thesis isn’t just blind faith—it’s based on the “Matthew effect” created by developer ecosystems. He observes that when the market shifts from frenzy back to rationality, capital and talent concentrate on already-validated infrastructure rather than scattering across many unproven new chains. This “concentration at the top” trend repeats in tech—Microsoft in the Windows era, and iOS/Android in the mobile internet era.

SOL’s rise represents another path: attracting developers through extreme performance and user experience, rather than relying on Ethereum’s “legitimacy.” The two routes can coexist, but they share one thing—both require time to build an ecosystem, not marketing-driven shortcuts.

💡 Impact on the Crypto Market

1. For ETH: the moat deepens further, and L2 and RWA narratives continue attracting institutional favor
2. For SOL: its benchmark status as a high-performance chain is reinforced, but watch out for how centralization controversies could hinder institutional adoption
3. For new L1s: 2026 may be the “year of falsification”—projects without real users and real capital inflows will face severe challenges

title: Capital Is Leaving the Sidelines and the Tape Knows Where It's Going
subTitle:
Picture a trading floor after lunch — the morning lull breaks, chairs swivel, screens light up, and suddenly everyone is moving at once. That is what today's crypto market feels like. After weeks of choppy, low-conviction trading, meaningful capital is finally rotating back into the majors, and the order flow is telling a clear story about where conviction is building.

Let's start with the numbers. According to CoinMarketCap data pulled today, $ETH is trading at $1,700.80 on Binance, up 5.25% over the past 24 hours with a daily volume of $680.70 million. That is not a lazy bounce — that is a volume-confirmed move. Meanwhile, $SOL sits at $80.68, posting a 24-hour gain of 4.32% on $315.12 million in volume. Together these two assets carry a combined market capitalization north of $250 billion, and when they both wake up in the same session, it usually means risk appetite is returning to the large-cap end of the market.

The rotation is not random. Look at what is driving the narrative. Aave just announced the deployment of its V3 lending protocol and the GHO stablecoin on Monad — a move that puts fresh DeFi infrastructure directly in front of Ethereum's liquidity base. Ondo Finance is expanding its tokenized equities product with onchain shareholder voting, pulling traditional finance rails deeper into smart-contract territory. The UK government released a payments blueprint that explicitly calls for tokenized payments within a "multi-money ecosystem." Each of these headlines funnels attention and capital toward the chains best positioned to absorb institutional-grade activity, and right now that spotlight sits squarely on $ETH and $SOL.

Now let's talk about the levels that matter, because this is where the story gets practical. On the $ETH side, the 72-hour support is $1,550.20 and the resistance overhead is $1,725.00. With price currently sitting at $1,700.80, ETH is knocking on the door of that resistance ceiling. If it pushes through $1,725.00 with sustained volume, the chart opens up and momentum buyers have room to operate. If price gets rejected here and slips back toward $1,550.20, that support becomes the line in the sand — holding it keeps the bullish structure intact, but losing it would flip the bias and hand control back to sellers. Tap $ETH to watch those levels play out in real time.

Over on $SOL, the setup is tighter and arguably cleaner. The 72-hour support sits at $71.90 and resistance caps at $82.78. Price at $80.68 is already in the upper half of that range, which tells you buyers have been accumulating. If SOL holds above $71.90 on any pullback, that is the dip-buy zone where defense has been solid. A decisive break above $82.78 would confirm continuation and likely pull fresh volume into the pair. If $71.90 gives way, the bullish thesis weakens quickly and traders will look for the next floor.

The broader tape reinforces this rotation thesis. Among today's notable movers on CoinMarketCap, M surged 53.7%, MAGMA climbed 44.6%, and B gained 20.9%. These kinds of sharp mid-cap pumps often signal that speculative capital is re-engaging — and historically, that speculative energy flows downstream into the majors once the initial froth settles.

So what does all of this mean for someone watching the charts right now? The market is shifting from a defensive posture into something more opportunistic. Institutional-adjacent developments in tokenized assets, lending, and regulatory frameworks are creating real catalysts, not just social-media hype. The capital rotation into $ETH and $SOL is grounded in fundamentals meeting flow, not blind momentum.

The question worth asking: are you watching where the money is actually going, or just where it was yesterday?

Read the tape, not the noise.
